headline: Maui County Public Works Commission

meeting.summary: The Public Works Commission conditionally approved street names, chose its 2025 chair and vice chair, and kept Wednesday 1:30 p.m. meetings.
meeting.recap: The Public Works Commission was called to order on October 30th, 2024, at 1:35 p.m.[[0:00:30]] The commission voted to approve the minutes of its last meeting.[[0:04:30]] Staff said all the proposed street names for a residential project are available for use.[[0:06:00]] With no Hawaiian language expert present, members approved the street names on the condition that the translation is validated.[[0:07:26]] Members received their annual training on the Sunshine Law (open meeting rules), ethics, and their duties.[[0:08:04]] Members heard that board business cannot be discussed between members outside a noticed public meeting unless the law allows it.[[0:09:18]] The commission was created by an ordinance in 2013 that combined several commissions into one.[[0:22:04]] Staff said the commission has three vacancies and two vacant alternate seats.[[0:27:00]] The commission voted to keep its current chair as chair for 2025.[[0:29:10]] A commissioner declined a nomination for vice chair, saying he wanted to give others a chance.[[0:30:36]] The commission voted to make another commissioner vice chair for the 2025 term.[[0:30:59]] The commission voted to keep meeting on Wednesdays at 1:30 p.m. in 2025.[[0:34:03]] The meeting ended at 2:10 p.m.[[0:34:46]]
decided: The commission approved the minutes of its last meeting by a show of hands.
The commission approved the street name application on the condition that the translation is validated.
The commission voted to keep its current chair as chair for 2025.
The commission voted to make another commissioner vice chair for the 2025 term.
The commission voted to keep meeting on Wednesdays at 1:30 p.m. in 2025.
meeting.next: The street names still need their translation validated by a Hawaiian language expert.
